objective: Structured top-level result summary on the main Research results page: active structures, dominant/no-dominant state, main conflict/no-conflict state, all visible without navigating away from ResearchRunPage.

canonical_research_response_already_had: dominant_alphas: DominantAlpha[] (alpha_id, alpha_name, activation_score, status, direction)
main_conflict: AlphaConflict | null (bull_structure/bear_structure each with alpha_id, alpha_name)
canonical_research_response_did_not_have: the full active-Alpha list (only dominant_alphas -- dominant OR regime_level -- was present, not active/capped_active Alphas)
pre_implementation_inspection_findings.conclusion: Parts B (Dominant Structure) and C (Main Conflict) required NO additional fetch -- both fully derivable from the CanonicalResearchResponse already loaded by useResearchRun on ResearchRunPage. Part A (Active Structures) required one additional fetch to the existing GET /api/research/{run_id}/graph endpoint (the same one StructureGraphPage already uses), reusing its already-established bucketForAlpha() classification logic verbatim rather than inventing a new definition of 'meaningfully active'.
pre_implementation_inspection_findings.human_readable_names: Already resolved server-side on every Alpha-bearing object (alpha_id + alpha_name always paired) -- no frontend taxonomy dictionary was created or needed.

frontend_added.purpose: The new top-level structural snapshot section: Active Structures, Dominant Structure, Main Conflict, each with explicit legitimate-result empty states and safe loading/error/not-ready states.
Lean, single-endpoint (GET /graph) hook with the same AbortController/run-mismatch-guard safety pattern as the project's existing hooks, used only by the Active Structures part of the new summary.
15 component tests covering every required demo state (see test_results below).

frontend_modified.change: Added one import and one conditional render of <StructuralSnapshot runId={runId} research={research} /> immediately after the existing Research summary panel and before the Data Quality / Analyst findings panels. +5 lines. No other line touched.

Exported the existing bucketForAlpha() function, AlphaLevelBucket type, and ALPHA_LEVEL_BUCKETS constant (added the `export` keyword to three already-existing, unmodified declarations) so StructuralSnapshot can reuse the exact same production Alpha-level classification -- zero behavioral change to StructureGraphPage itself. +10/-4 lines (all `export` keyword additions plus one clarifying comment).

Appended a new, additive CSS block (+100 lines) for the structural-snapshot-* classes, reusing existing design tokens (--space-*, --color-*, --radius-*, --font-size-*) and the existing 3-column-to-1-column responsive collapse pattern already used elsewhere in the file. No existing rule was modified.

api_calls_reused: GET /api/research/{run_id} (already fetched by useResearchRun on ResearchRunPage) -- source of dominant_alphas and main_conflict, no new fetch

GET /api/research/{run_id}/graph (already used by StructureGraphPage; now also fetched independently by the new useResearchGraph hook on ResearchRunPage, following the project's existing per-page-fetch convention) -- source of the full active-Alpha list

active_structures: error (safe copy, retry button, no raw exception)
completed-empty (legitimate: 'No Alpha structure currently meets the active threshold.')
completed-populated (chip list, ID + human name, bucket order preserved from StructureGraphPage)
dominant_structure: legitimate-empty ('No single structure currently dominates.' + explanatory sentence)
present (one or more Alphas, each ID + human name)
main_conflict: legitimate-empty (adapted from ConflictRadarPage's own approved no-conflict copy)
present (both sides' ID + human name, 'vs' separator, link to Conflict Radar)

terminology_check.note: Alpha IDs are always paired with a human-readable name in the new summary; internal level vocabulary (active/capped_active/dominant/regime_level/candidate) is used only to bucket which Alphas appear in Part A, never rendered as a label in the new summary itself. This is a local, scoped translation -- P1-2 (app-wide jargon cleanup) is explicitly not attempted here.
